title: ₹20,000 Extra? Personal Loan Prepayment vs. SIP Investment
description: When faced with an extra ₹20,000 monthly, choosing between personal loan prepayment and SIP investment is a common dilemma. Prepaying a high-interest personal.

faq.q: Is there any tax benefit on personal loan interest?
faq.a: Generally, no. Unlike home loans, where interest paid can be deducted under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, personal loan interest does not offer any direct tax benefits.

faq.q: What if my SIP returns are very high?
faq.a: While SIPs can deliver high returns, especially in bull markets, these are not guaranteed. The decision to prepay a loan offers a guaranteed saving at the loan's interest rate, which is a risk-free return.

faq.q: Should I prepay if I have an emergency fund shortage?
faq.a: No, it's crucial to build a robust emergency fund first. Without it, you might be forced to take another high-interest loan during an unforeseen financial crisis, negating any benefits of prepayment.

faq.q: Does part-prepayment reduce EMI or tenure?
faq.a: Typically, part-prepayment reduces the loan tenure, keeping the EMI constant, which helps you become debt-free faster. However, some lenders might offer the option to reduce the EMI while keeping the tenure constant. You should clarify this with your lender.

faq.q: What about other high-interest debts like credit card outstanding?
faq.a: Credit card outstanding balances often carry significantly higher interest rates than personal loans. If you have credit card debt, prioritising its repayment should be your first financial goal.

faq.q: Are there prepayment charges on personal loans?
faq.a: Many banks levy a prepayment penalty on personal loans, especially if you prepay within a certain period or clear the loan entirely before its tenure. Always check your loan agreement for these clauses.
